analysis:
Examined MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (head lines 529-1608) and the new ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift. The only changed hunk in the scheduler is at head 828-835: tokenize() now receives promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil. This partitions the new prompt-token cache by the same coordinator-authored cacheScope used for the prefix KV cache, so it is consistent with the T-041 scoping (cacheSalt derived from authenticated account, model, contract). requestCacheScope and cacheEnabled are defined outside the supplied excerpt, and the PromptTokenCache implementation (storage, persistence, key derivation, eviction) is not supplied. I could not verify whether that cache holds prompt-derived data at rest or in memory, so the T-041 cross-tenant concern stays an open integration question. If cacheEnabled is false the scope is nil, so token reuse is presumably disabled; I did not see how nil is handled inside the cache. The media path (lines 565-808) and the native MiMo path (1015-1085) show no change. The native MiMo path passes cacheScope and cacheEnabled:false, which is unchanged.

ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift is new and not yet wired in the supplied code. Its call site (PromptTokenCache) is not supplied. It does verbatim, exactly-once string replacement on served chat templates for Gemma4 and GPT-OSS to cut quadratic loops. The rewrites apply only if the old blocks match once and the introduced names are absent, otherwise they return nil (fail-safe). Header comments say the render is compared against the unmodified template at load and in sampled checks, and the env kill switch is DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS. The rewrite logic looks semantically plausible: tracking the previous non-tool role, break after stopped, and the last-final-index precomputation. Possible divergence in Jinja scoping or in whether `break` is supported by swift-jinja is correctness risk, not a security regression. Template content is operator/model-supplied, not consumer-controlled.

Next pass should check PromptTokenCache for scope keying, tenant isolation, on-disk persistence and TTFT oracle exposure.
